measure_hint: Start PyMOL's Measurement wizard: click two atoms for a distance
measure_locked_other_wizard: Another wizard is open in PyMOL: close it first
preset_note_ligand_site: Ligand site: the target is your selection (sele), else the previous target, else the only ligand. When none decides it, nothing changes and PyMOL says why at its top left. Otherwise every atom's representations are hidden, and only these are shown again: the target and the residues within 5 Å (side chains and CA) as sticks, the target's carbons in yellow and the other elements in their own colours, waters in that range as spheres, polar contacts as dashes, labels with residue name, number and chain, and the protein as a cartoon. Everything else stays hidden, metal ions and other ligands near the target included. Cartoon transparency is set to half for the whole scene.
preset_note_pocket: Pocket surface: the target is your selection (sele), else the previous target, else the only ligand. When none decides it, nothing changes and PyMOL says why at its top left. Otherwise every surface is hidden except that of the residues within 6 Å of the target, and the target shows as sticks, its carbons in yellow and the other elements in their own colours; other representations stay as they were. Surface transparency is set to half and two-sided lighting turned on for the whole scene, not only for this surface.
preset_note_bfactor: B-factor: blue = low (well placed), white = middle, red = high (mobile). The colour range is that of the backbone CA atoms. A structure with no CA atoms, or with the same value on every CA, is left as it is, and PyMOL says why at its top left.
preset_note_plddt: pLDDT: dark blue = above 90 (very high), light blue = 70-90 (confident), yellow = 50-70 (low), orange = below 50 (very low). A structure with no CA atoms, or whose CA values all lie between 0 and 1 (not a pLDDT on the 0-100 scale), is left as it is, and PyMOL says why at its top left.
preset_note_publication: Publication: white background, no shadows, no fog, smooth edges. Save the image with “Ray-trace and save”.
preset_note_reset: Every molecule is drawn again in the usual representations of a load — cartoon for protein, sticks for ligands, spheres for ions, lines and crosses for water — with each element in its own colour and carbons in the molecule's colour. This is not a record of how the structure or session first looked: labels and surfaces you added go, and the view frames the whole structure. The background goes back to black, and these nine settings to PyMOL's defaults, values you set yourself included: transparency, cartoon transparency, two-sided lighting, shadows, depth cue, ray-trace fog, antialiasing, ray-trace opaque background and fancy helices. Other settings stay as they are. The dashes and selections Drug discovery made are gone; density meshes and other measurements stay.
cmd_placeholder: Type a command and press Enter (↑↓ for history; a multi-line paste runs line by line)
cmd_err_too_long: The command is too long (at most {{limit}} characters).
cmd_err_session_load: A shared session (.pse) cannot be loaded from the command line.
cmd_paste_refused: Nothing was run: pasted line {{line}} cannot be sent. {{detail}}
cmd_paste_stopped: Stopped at line {{done}} of {{total}} pasted lines: {{detail}}
cmd_stopped_dropped_one: The command was stopped; the {{n}} line waiting was not sent.
cmd_stopped_dropped_other: The command was stopped; the {{n}} lines waiting were not sent.
cmd_gone_dropped_one: The command did not finish: {{detail}}. The {{n}} line waiting was not sent.
cmd_gone_dropped_other: The command did not finish: {{detail}}. The {{n}} lines waiting were not sent.
busy_cancel_note: PyMOL cannot interrupt a running request, so PyMOL is rebuilt and the last checkpoint restored; changes after it may be lost. With no checkpoint, the structure is reloaded and changes since it opened may be lost (the view is put back).
settings_scale_note: Change this if PyMOL's text looks too small or too large at a Windows display scale such as 125 % or 150 %. Kept in this browser only.
settings_set_note: Current values are not shown here (nothing is read out of the PyMOL frame). Run get <name> in the command line to see one in PyMOL's own output.
keys_note: Chrome on Windows takes these PyMOL shortcuts for itself, so they never reach this page. Press them with Alt added instead, after clicking into the PyMOL view. On other systems the desktop may take the chord with Alt added first (Ctrl+Alt+T or Ctrl+Alt+F4 on Linux, for example). On a keyboard layout that types characters with AltGr, the same keys pressed with AltGr also reach PyMOL as these shortcuts.
keys_tab: Tab / Shift+Tab: move focus out of the PyMOL view (not sent to PyMOL).
keys_escape: Esc: toggles PyMOL's text panel (as in PyMOL).
keys_function: F1-F12: recall PyMOL's scenes F1-F12 (as in PyMOL).
ray_button_note_v2: Opens the settings (size, resolution, rendering mode, shadows and more). The image downloads at once and is also stored in the structure page's "Screenshot/pose history". In the browser it takes seconds to minutes; Stop cancels it.
ray_dialog_note: PyMOL ray-traces the current view with these settings. The image downloads as soon as it is ready and is stored in the screenshot/pose history.
ray_size_scale_over: {{n}}x the view ({{w}} × {{h}} px, over the {{max}} px limit)
ray_size_custom: Width and height of your own
ray_side_invalid: Enter whole numbers from 1 to {{max}} for both sides.
ray_aspect_note: Its aspect ratio is not the view's, so the image frames a different part of the scene than the screen.
ray_quality_normal_note: Quick: no antialiasing, no shadows, 150 dpi.
ray_quality_high_note: For print: high antialiasing, shadows, 300 dpi.
ray_dpi_note: The dpi is written into the image for printing; it does not change the number of pixels.
ray_size_unmeasured: The view has not been laid out yet, so only the view's own size can be used.
ray_size_too_large: {{w}} x {{h}} px is too large: each side can be at most {{max}} px. Choose a smaller size.
ray_time_note_v2: A larger size or high antialiasing takes longer: 2x the view takes about 4 times as long as the view's size, and high antialiasing several times more. A ray that runs past 10 minutes is stopped, and PyMOL is restarted from its last automatic snapshot.
ray_time_slow: This may take about {{min}} minutes or more.
ray_time_risky: This may take about {{min}} minutes or more and could pass the 10-minute limit. Past it the ray is stopped and PyMOL is restarted, which can undo recent changes. Pick a smaller size or lower antialiasing to be safe.
ray_create_not_ready: PyMOL is not ready (it is starting, restarting or saving another image). Create becomes available when it is ready.
detail_network: no answer came from the server
detail_unreadable: the server's answer could not be read
detail_frame_gone: the PyMOL view was rebuilt or closed
detail_export_refused: what PyMOL sent back had the wrong shape, so it was not taken
detail_export_expired: PyMOL's answer came after its deadline, so it was not taken
export_note_v2: Saves atoms now in PyMOL to this computer as a PDB, mmCIF, SDF or MOL2 file. The coordinates are those of the current state (the one shown). The file is not sent anywhere.
export_target_sele_note: What you selected in PyMOL by clicking or dragging over atoms.
export_target_all: Everything (including hidden objects, added structures and docking poses)
export_target_ligand: Ligands (PyMOL's organic: small molecules, no water or ions)
export_custom_note: For example “resn LIG”, “chain A and organic” or “byres (organic around 5)”. One line of ASCII, up to {{max}} characters.
export_custom_invalid: Write the selection as one line of ASCII letters, digits and symbols, up to {{max}} characters.
export_format_cif: mmCIF (for proteins and complexes, including ones too large for PDB)
export_format_mol2: MOL2 (for small molecules, with atom types)
export_small_note: Bond orders and charges in an SDF or MOL2 file are as PyMOL read them. Nothing is added or corrected. A ligand read from a structure file (PDB, mmCIF) usually carries no bond orders, so its bonds are all written as single bonds.
export_why_busy: The next export can start once this one has finished.
export_why_custom_invalid: The selection you wrote cannot be sent. Correct it as the note under the field says.
export_err_too_large: It is over {{limit}} MiB and cannot be exported. Narrow the selection.
export_err_not_file: What PyMOL returned was not a {{format}} file, so nothing was saved.
export_err_no_sele: There is no current selection (sele). Click or drag over atoms in PyMOL, then press again.
export_err_unknown_selection: PyMOL could not read this selection: {{detail}}
export_err_unknown_selection_bare: PyMOL could not read this selection.
export_withdrawn: Molecule export withdrawn: the dialog closed before PyMOL got to it, so no file was saved.
export_why_close_busy: PyMOL is running a request, so this dialog cannot close. “{{stop}}” rebuilds PyMOL and cancels this export; anything waiting stops too.
export_waiting_note: The export has not started: PyMOL is finishing a load requested earlier (for example an added structure, a pose, a density map or a session). This wait cannot be stopped, but you can close the dialog; the export is then withdrawn and no file is saved.
export_queued_note: The export has not started: PyMOL is still running a request made earlier. You can close the dialog; the export is then withdrawn, no file is saved and nothing in PyMOL is lost.
pse_export_note: Saves everything now in PyMOL — the structures, how they are shown, the selections, the scenes and the settings — as one session file (.pse) on this computer. Desktop PyMOL opens it. The file is not sent anywhere.
pse_export_warn: Desktop PyMOL can run code inside a .pse file when it opens one. This file is made fresh by PyMOL from what it holds now; still, open a .pse you receive only when it comes from someone you trust.
pse_export_err_not_file: PyMOL returned no session data, so nothing was saved.
pse_export_err_too_large: The session is larger than {{limit}} MiB and cannot be saved.
pse_export_waiting_note: The save has not started: PyMOL is finishing a load requested earlier (for example an added structure, a pose, a density map or a session). This wait cannot be stopped, but you can close the dialog; the save is then withdrawn and no file is saved.
pse_export_queued_note: The save has not started: PyMOL is still running a request made earlier. You can close the dialog; the save is then withdrawn, no file is saved and nothing in PyMOL is lost.
pse_export_withdrawn: Session save withdrawn: the dialog closed before PyMOL got to it, so no file was saved.
